heuristics: H1: the class-level r-adding walk with 2^16 adders behaves as a random mapping on the (r-1)/2 negation classes, up to an exponent penalty of at most 4/2^16. Used only for the collision statistics (proof.md 2.6).

M1: the class data read by the walk (the class key, which fixes the adder index, the 64-bit filter bits and the distinguished-point test, and the canonical sign) are independent uniform values, one per class, independent of x. P-256 has no canonical rotation and no exact-k fallback (measurement/step.c). Derivation: proof.md 2.0. From M1 and exact algebra: the escape depth and the order of 2 (2.1, D1, with ord_r(2) > 2 TRAIL_MAX verified for this r), the degenerate-pair and within-trail bound (2.2, Lemma G, DELTA_LOOP), the closure rates (2.3, Lemma C': 2-cycles at exactly 1/(2A), odd lengths never close structurally, 3..64 at most 3/A^2), the abandonment bound (2.4, Lemma T': first moment, DELTA_ABANDON) and the metered-work reserve (2.5, Lemma M').

M2: a premise on the table. The table and the walk coins come from one stream, random.Random(1): seed 1 is a constant of the specification, chosen without reference to the target. One draw randrange(1, r) is discarded (the test generator's target), then each point takes two draws randrange(r): the first 2^16 pairs are the adders (c_i, d_i), the next 2^16 the walk starts (the trail coins), and 1024 spares. The coefficients are a function of the seed alone, not of the target's value, and they are the measured inputs (walk_ref.py gen, seeds 1 and 2). They are treated as independent uniform values in Z_r, independent of the uniform target x. Not proved; used in 2.2 and 2.3 (proof.md 2.0).
limitations: The model success term is 0.411524 at tau = 0.5303, 0.0215 above 0.39. After the 1/64 meter loss, 2^-20 and the failure terms DELTA_LOOP, DELTA_ABANDON and DELTA_TAIL (about 1e-16 together), the bound is 0.395898 (proof.md 2.6).
M1 carries the success bound. It is not proved for this walk; the whole procedure is tested only on toy curves at theta = 2^-5, which cannot test the production regime.

The escape depth is bounded per step (K_ESC = TRAIL_MAX), so D1 needs ord_r(2) > 2 TRAIL_MAX. This is verified for the P-256 order from the smooth part S = (r-1)/C2 of r-1 (proof.md 2.1, accounting.py); the 188-bit cofactor is not factored and is not needed.
DELTA_LOOP, DELTA_TAIL and DELTA_ABANDON are union bounds from the stated counts. They are upper bounds, not rates measured in any run.

H3 is a measurement assumption, not a probabilistic heuristic: the Callgrind instruction counts on production inputs represent the common path, 833.61 (plain) and 843.61 (anchor, rare events removed) instructions per walk step, plus at most 3 for the first distinguished-point test (C_COMMON = 847). The rare paths are out of line and charged at worst case, and the Markov reserve covers the expected rare work.
Analytic production cost; no production-size execution.
Needs about 2^68.5 stored distinguished points; not a practical attack.
The whole procedure, including resolution, is tested only on toy curves.
Distinguished points never occur in a production-parameter measurement sample; the restart and abandonment paths were checked on small builds.

The rare-path charges are forced-path maxima measured with a bounding build (proof.md section 3.1); the bounding build is checked for equality and for dominance on the forced paths, not proved for every input.
The work meter's abort probability, 1/64, is a Markov bound on the expected metered rare work (Lemma M', proof.md 2.5), and is counted in delta.
